prompts.CARD_WRITE:
You are writing ONE skill card for a weaker terminal agent on Terminal Bench V2.1.
The card teaches one subtask type. It will be listed in the agent's skill
catalog on DIFFERENT TB21 tasks, not the tasks below, and the agent
opens it when its situation matches the card's "when to use" text.

SUBTASK TYPE: <type_name>
ENTRY STATE (what the agent observes when this subtask starts):
<entry_state>

HOW THE STRONG MODEL DID IT (successful segments of this type; SOURCE and
SUBTASK_SUCCESS describe each segment):
<strong_segments>

WHERE THE WEAK MODEL FAILED AT IT (failed segments of this type from the
latest trials; "(none)" when there are none):
<weak_segments>

ENVIRONMENT PROTOCOL (what the agent sees and may do at each step; every
step you write must be executable under it):
<protocol>

THE PLAYBOOK THE AGENT ALREADY SEES AT EVERY STEP ("(none)" when it has
none):
<playbook>

<profile_section>

Read the weak model profile FIRST. Every step must be an action this exact
model can carry out as written. Where the profile names a weakness, add an
explicit guard.

Write the card so that it adds only what the playbook does not already
give: the procedure for this subtask, the checks that tell it worked, and
the mistakes the failed segments show. Never repeat a playbook rule.

- when_to_use: the subtask's observable entry state, in terms the agent can
  check from what it sees (file types, input structure, error text). Do not describe a moment
  in time and do not use task names.
- steps: 3 to 7 steps, as a list without numbers. A step is one decision:
  "When <observable condition>, do <general action>; verify <pass signal>;
  if it fails, <fallback>." Use only actions the segments support.
- every task-specific value is a <placeholder> in angle brackets: file
  names, paths, commands, flags, API names, constants, error strings,
  entities;
- a command may appear only in a general form that works after substituting
  the placeholders;
- scripts used as tools: write only the invocation pattern, the inputs, and
  the expected output—never include the script body, even if the trajectory
  showed it in full;
- code as the deliverable (when the task is to write a program or module):
  describe the structure the code must satisfy and how to verify it with
  the task's tests—do not include the implementation;
- not_applicable_when: observable signs that this card is wrong for the
  situation.
- summary: one line, a verb and an object, saying what the card teaches. No
  trigger and no task names.

Keep the card short: under 1,500 characters in total. Use only complete
sentences.

<correction_note>Output ONLY JSON with exactly these fields:
{"when_to_use": "<the observable entry state of the subtask>",
  "steps": ["<one decision: condition, action, verify, fallback>", "..."],
  "not_applicable_when": "<observable conditions under which this card is wrong>",
  "summary": "<one line: what this card teaches>"}
prompts.REVISE_CONTENT:
A skill card written for a weaker terminal agent on Terminal Bench V2.1 did not help: in
the real trials below the agent opened it before the step where the trial
went wrong, and still failed. This is a Terminal Bench V2.1 skill; it will be used
on other tasks, so task-specific details must not enter it. Rewrite ONLY
the content: the steps and the "do not use when" text. The summary and the
"when to use" text stay exactly as they are.

ENVIRONMENT PROTOCOL (what the agent sees and may do at each step):
<protocol>

THE CARD (current version):
<skill_card>

THE PLAYBOOK THE AGENT SEES AT EVERY STEP ("(none)" when it has none):
<playbook>

THE REAL STEPS (from where the agent opened the card to just after the step
where the trial went wrong, per failed trial):
<evidence_steps>

DIAGNOSES OF THE FAILURES:
<diagnosis>

<profile_section>

Rewrite the content so that an agent following it, in these situations and
in any situation of the same kind, does not make the mistakes the diagnoses
name. Read the profile first: guard against the weaknesses it names.
- steps: 3 to 7 steps, as a list without numbers. A step is one decision:
  "When <observable condition>, do <general action>; verify <pass signal>;
  if it fails, <fallback>." Compress instead of appending.
- every task-specific value is a <placeholder> in angle brackets: file
  names, paths, commands, flags, API names, constants, error strings,
  entities;
- a command may appear only in a general form that works after substituting
  the placeholders;
- scripts used as tools: write only the invocation pattern, the inputs, and
  the expected output—never include the script body, even if the trajectory
  showed it in full;
- code as the deliverable (when the task is to write a program or module):
  describe the structure the code must satisfy and how to verify it with
  the task's tests—do not include the implementation;
- weave the discipline into the verify and fallback parts of the steps:
  check before acting, read the error before retrying, run the verifier before calling mark_task_complete.
- not_applicable_when: the observable signs that this card is wrong for the
  situation.
- Add only what the playbook does not already give; never repeat a
  playbook rule.
- Keep the card's idea; change wording, order, granularity or missing steps.
  Never copy names, values or entities from the trials: they become
  <placeholders>.
- Keep the whole card under 1,500 characters.

Output ONLY JSON:
{"steps": ["<one decision: condition, action, verify, fallback>", "..."],
  "not_applicable_when": "<observable conditions under which this card is wrong>",
  "revision_reason": "<one sentence: what you changed and why>"}
prompts.REVISE_TRIGGER:
A skill card written for a weaker terminal agent on Terminal Bench V2.1 was not opened
when it was needed: in the real trials below the agent was doing the
subtask the card teaches, never opened the card before the step where the
trial went wrong, and failed. Rewrite ONLY the trigger: the one-line summary
and the "when to use" text. The agent sees one line per card in its skill
catalog, made of these two fields, and decides from that line alone whether
to open the card. The steps of the card stay exactly as they are.

ENVIRONMENT PROTOCOL (what the agent sees and may do at each step):
<protocol>

CURRENT SUMMARY: <current_summary>
CURRENT WHEN TO USE: <current_when_to_use>

THE SKILL CATALOG THE AGENT SAW:
<skill_catalog>

THE PLAYBOOK THE AGENT SAW AT EVERY STEP ("(none)" when it had none):
<playbook>

THE REAL STEPS (from the start of the subtask to the step where the trial
went wrong, per failed trial):
<evidence_steps>

DIAGNOSES OF THE FAILURES:
<diagnosis>

<profile_section>

Write a new summary and when_to_use so that an agent in these situations,
and in any situation of the same kind, recognizes this card and opens it,
an agent in an unrelated situation does not, and the line stays
distinguishable from the other lines in the catalog.
- summary: one sentence, a verb and an object, saying what the card
  teaches. No trigger, no task or subtask names.
- when_to_use: the observable entry state of the subtask, named by the
  signs the agent can see at that moment (file types, input structure, error text). Do not
  describe a moment in time.
- Do not copy names, values or entities from the trials: describe the kind
  of situation.
- Summary and when_to_use together stay under about 400 characters and never
  over 1,000. Write only complete sentences.

Output ONLY JSON:
{"summary": "<one line: what the card teaches>",
  "when_to_use": "<the observable entry state>",
  "revision_reason": "<one sentence: what you changed and why>"}
prompts.SEGMENT:
You are given the view of one agent trajectory from Terminal Bench V2.1.
Split it into capability-coherent sub-procedures.

TRAJECTORY:
<trajectory_view>

A segment is one reusable sub-procedure, not one task-specific step. A good
segment has:
- an observable trigger: the situation where the sub-procedure starts;
- a general goal: what it achieves, stated without this task's names or
  concrete values;
- a boundary: the point where the next sub-procedure begins.

Split the trajectory into at most <K> such subtasks.

Rules:
- The segments must cover the whole trajectory in order, without gaps and
  without overlaps: the first segment starts at step 0, the last one ends at
  the final step, and consecutive segments touch (the end index of one is
  the start index of the next; end indices are exclusive). Every step must
  belong to exactly one segment.
- Use at most <K> segments, and every segment must contain at least one step.
- Merge adjacent steps that belong to the same capability. Environment
  setup, one-off commands, and task-specific data wrangling should be folded
  into the nearest capability segment, not given their own segment; their
  steps still belong to a segment (so coverage stays complete), but the
  segment's label and description name the capability, not the setup.
- If the natural capability boundaries number more than <K>, merge the most
  closely related segments first; prefer folding setup or discovery steps
  into a real capability segment over merging two distinct capabilities.
- Do not restate the content of the steps. Describe each segment at the
  level of its observable trigger and general goal, so the step content and
  the segment description stay separate.
- "label" is a short capability phrase, not a task-specific phrase (for
  example "build and verify a source project", "recover a key from known
  pairs").
- "description" is one or two sentences that name the observable trigger and
  the general goal.
- "success" says whether that segment's own goal was achieved by the end of
  the segment, independent of whether the overall trajectory succeeded.

Return ONLY a JSON array, one object per segment in order, with exactly
these fields:
[
  {"start": <first step index, integer>,
    "end": <step index after the last step of this segment, exclusive, integer>,
    "label": "<short capability phrase>",
    "description": "<one or two sentences: observable trigger and general goal>",
    "success": <true or false>}
]
Return no text before or after the JSON array.
prompts.SUBTASK_TYPING:
You sort segments of terminal-agent trajectories on Terminal Bench V2.1 into
subtask types. A subtask type is one recurring part of a task that a weaker
agent can learn as a unit, such as finding a needed object or recovering
from a rejected action. It is defined by its observable entry state: what
the agent can see at the moment the subtask starts (file types, input structure, error text).
It is not a moment in time ("at task start", "before finishing") and not a
task name.

EXISTING SUBTASK TYPES (type id | name | entry state; "(none)" when the
table is empty):
<type_table>

SEGMENTS TO SORT (SOURCE names the model that ran the segment, strong or
weak; SUBTASK_SUCCESS says whether the segment reached its own goal):
<cards>

Rules:
- Put every SUBTASK_ID from the segments exactly once.
- Never invent a SUBTASK_ID and never repeat one.
- Prefer an existing type whenever the segment does the same part of the
  task from the same kind of entry state, even when task names, objects or
  files differ. A failed segment belongs to the type of the part it was
  trying to do.
- Declare a new type only when no existing type fits. Give it a short key
  of your own ("new1", "new2", ...), a name (a verb and an object, no task
  names) and its entry state (one sentence naming what the agent can
  observe when this subtask starts). Several segments may share a new
  type.
- The "type" of an assignment is either an existing type id from the table
  or the key of a new type declared in this reply.

<correction_note>Output ONLY JSON with exactly this shape:
{"new_types": [
  {"key": "<new1>", "name": "<verb and object>",
    "entry_state": "<what the agent observes when this subtask starts>"}
 ],
 "assignments": [
  {"subtask_id": "<exact SUBTASK_ID from the segments>",
    "type": "<an existing type id or a new type key>"}
 ]}
prompts.TRIAL_FAILURE_ANALYSIS:
You analyze ONE failed trial of a weaker terminal agent on Terminal Bench V2.1.
Your job is diagnosis: say why the trial failed and where.

ENVIRONMENT PROTOCOL (what the agent sees and may do at each step; it is
fixed, and every executor already receives it):
<protocol>

TASK:
<task_instruction>

PLAYBOOK THE AGENT SAW (shown at every step; "(none)" when it had none):
<playbook>

SKILL CATALOG THE AGENT SAW (one line per card it could open; "(none)" when
it ran without skills):
<skill_catalog>

SKILL CARDS THE AGENT OPENED (the full text it read; "(none)" when it opened
none):
<opened_skills>

THE TRIAL (the agent's commands and what each returned, step by step,
numbered from 0; opening a skill card is a step too):
<trial_steps>

The trial failed.

Explain why it failed. Use only evidence visible above; if the cause is
unclear, say what is unclear instead of inventing certainty.

Then give:
- failing_step: the number of the ONE step where the trial went decisively
  wrong (the first step after which success was no longer reachable without
  undoing something). It must be an integer from 0 to <last_step>.
- scope: "subtask" when the mistake belongs to one part of the task (finding
  something, transforming it, checking a result, recovering from a rejected
  command); "general" when it belongs to no part in particular (a
  wrong reply format, repeating the same command without progress,
  giving up early).
- model_note: a weakness of the model this failure shows (a habit, a
  misreading, a missing check), stated so that it holds beyond this task.
  Empty when the failure says nothing general about the model.
- playbook_note: a working practice that would have prevented this failure
  and holds for every task of the benchmark. Not a step recipe for one kind
  of task, not a fact of this task, and nothing the protocol already states.
  Empty when no such practice exists.

<correction_note>Output ONLY JSON:
{"reason": "<a clear paragraph explaining the failure>",
  "failing_step": <integer from 0 to <last_step>>,
  "scope": "<subtask or general>",
  "model_note": "<one or two sentences, or an empty string>",
  "playbook_note": "<one or two sentences, or an empty string>"}

no_profile_section: No weak-model profile is provided. Treat the reader as a generally capable terminal agent: every step must be a concrete action it can carry out, one action per step. Do not assume any specific weakness.
